newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally higher on very light demand and light to moderate offerings, USDA said.
Demand for retail and HRI needs was rather light, after last week's large volume of trading, which has yet to clear the retail counter.
Higher price levels early in the week, coupled with the Lenten season, also played big roles in the light demand.
Rib, loin and round cuts traded higher during the trading period but round cuts ended the period on a weak undertone.

Chuck cuts encountered resistance at the higher price levels as inventories on these cuts were quite a burden. Closely trimmed items followed somewhat the same pattern as the commodity product as most cuts traded higher, except for some chuck cuts, which struggled to trade at steady levels.
Trade on beef trimmings was generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were steady to weak on light to moderate demand and offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 3.50 to 6.50 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.50 to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 2.00 to 4.50 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.00 higher; Beef trimmings generally steady; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 3.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.32 at 104.24; 700/850 Up 1.66 at 103.59; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.79 at 99.02; 700/850 Up 2.24 at 98.60.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The marketing of slaughter cows this week was uneven, as receipts in the south central area continue to be very light and numbers in the southeast and northern regions increased slightly compared to recent weeks.
The lean boneless beef market continued to feel the pressure from light demand and moderate offerings and traded at lower price levels.

The cow carcass market traded generally steady on light offerings and light to moderate demand. In addition, the 100% lean market remained strong as supplies and offerings were very light and buyers struggled to find product for their needs. Utility and Cutter carcasses steady; 90% boneless beef 4.00-5.00 lower; 85% 2.50-4.00 lower; 75% weak; 65% mostly 2.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, March 20, 1997 was estimated at 78.62 per cwt., dn 2.70 from a week ago Friday.
